points.heading: First conjugation (-ar / cantar)
points.body:
Main idea: A Spanish verb names an action. To conjugate means to change it for the person who acts. An infinitive is the dictionary form, such as cantar. The stem is what remains after -ar, and the ending is the part we add. Cantar belongs to the -ar family.

Explore: In cantar, cant- is the stem. Cant- plus -o makes yo canto; plus -as makes tú cantas; plus -a makes él canta. Hablar follows the same pattern: hablo, hablas, habla.

Practice: First explain the idea in your own words. Then split estudiar into its stem and ending. Write yo estudio, tú estudias, and él estudia. Then write one sentence with Yo estudio.

Common mistake: Do not write yo cantar. That is the dictionary form; yo canto tells who acts.

points.heading: Second conjugation (-er / comer)
points.body:
Main idea: Comer is an infinitive in the Spanish -er family. Its stem is com-, and its present endings for yo, tú, and él are -o, -es, and -e.

Explore: Com- plus -o makes yo como; plus -es makes tú comes; plus -e makes él come. Beber works in the same way: bebo, bebes, bebe.

Practice: First explain the idea in your own words. Then conjugate beber and leer for yo, tú, and él. Write one sentence with él bebe.

Common mistake: Do not use -as from cantar here. T comes ends in -es.

points.heading: Third conjugation (-ir / vivir)
points.body:
Main idea: Vivir is an infinitive in the Spanish -ir family. Its stem is viv-, and its present endings for yo, tú, and él are -o, -es, and -e.

Explore: Viv- plus -o makes yo vivo; plus -es makes tú vives; plus -e makes él vive. Escribir follows the same route: escribo, escribes, escribe.

Practice: First explain the idea in your own words. Then conjugate abrir and vivir for yo, tú, and él. Mark each stem and circle each ending.

Common mistake: Do not call a verb -er just because tú ends in -es. Check the infinitive first.

lesson.summary: In this lesson, you will use Spanish verb endings to say who does an action. Review: This week you learned to recognize the Spanish -ar, -er, and -ir families and to conjugate cantar, comer, and vivir for yo, tú, and él.
